title: September-October temperature balance gave no clear link to beech colour-to-fall gaps in four Swiss samples in 1961-2020
abstract: We tested the link between October minus September temperature and beech leaf fall minus leaf colour dates at a fixed two-month mean. We used 3,849 paired records at 85 Swiss stations in western and eastern samples in 1961-1990 and 1991-2020. The four slopes ranged from -0.20 to +0.33 days per C. All four corrected intervals included zero. Station trends, equal row weights and exclusion of negative gaps left all ordinary gap intervals across zero. Both phase dates had negative balance slopes in all four samples. Thus, phase shifts did not establish a change in their gap. Missing visits, coarse weather, selected long records and one national network limit inference. Fixed calendar weather can occur after the event. We infer no causal climate or pollution effect. Code, exact input hashes, aggregate results, numerical checks and a figure support reproduction.
